turns.query: Our oxygen sensor is coming up on its yearly recalibration per the vendor sheet, which gives no steps at all. What am I calibrating it against out here, and how do I set that up?

relevant.evidence:
The main goal of the one-point
DO calibration procedure is to create a 100-percent saturated
oxygen environment in which the DO sensor and its thermistor
are at the same temperature.
relevant.locator: Section 2.2 Calibration of Optical Sensors — "One-point calibration" / "Two-point calibration"

relevant.evidence:
Insert the sensor into the chamber per manufacturer’s
instructions to ensure 100-percent humidity.
relevant.locator: Procedure 1—Calibration in Air — "Wet the inside of the calibration chamber"

relevant.evidence:
For DO calibrations, the ambient atmospheric pressure
must be determined to the nearest 1 millimeter (mm) of
mercury.
relevant.locator: Section 2.2.1 Correction for Atmospheric Pressure and Salinity / 2.2.2 Selection of Calibration Method — "It is required that the barometric pressure be measured at the altitude of the DO calibration"

relevant.evidence:
Verify that the instrument reading is within ±0.2 mg/L or
2 percent of the computed saturation value, or use more
relevant.locator: Procedure 1—Calibration in Air, steps 7–9 / Variation of Procedure 1 — "within ±0.2 mg/L or 2 percent of the computed saturation value"

relevant.evidence: Calibrated specific-conductance sensor, if measurement is being made in a saline or brackish system
relevant.locator: Table 6.2–1, Equipment and supplies for the optical sensor method — "DO instrument should have a digital temperature and DO readout display"

relevant.evidence:
Correcting DO solubility for saline waters (specific
conductance greater than 2,000 μS/cm) varies with instru-
ment type, calibration method, and the salts in solution.
relevant.locator: Section 3.3 step 11-12, Section 4.0 Reporting, and Section 5.0 opening — "reported to the nearest 0.1 mg/L and stored to the nearest 0.01 mg/L"
